title: Thank you for participating in our survey.
body:
Please read and agree to our consent form:

DESCRIPTION: You are invited to participate in a research study exploring large language models’ (LLMs) behaviors. The study involves talking with a chatbot about an interpersonal conflict you experienced, and then answering some questions about the conflict and the model. The purpose of this research is to gain insights into different LLM behaviors.

TIME INVOLVEMENT: Your participation will take approximately twenty minutes.

RISKS AND BENEFITS: This study involves minimal physical risk, but it does include relevant interpersonal risks. Because you will be discussing a real conflict from your life with an AI chatbot, you may experience emotional discomfort during or after the interaction. Additionally, the chatbot may respond in ways that feel persuasive—even if those responses reflect poor judgment or discourage you from taking responsible actions. These behaviors are part of the study’s design and do not reflect guidance you should follow in your own life. All data will be stored securely in compliance with Stanford University data protection standards. While your participation will help improve understanding of AI behavior in social contexts, there are no guaranteed personal benefits.

PAYMENTS: Upon completion, you will receive $2 USD as payment for your participation in this study.

PARTICIPANT’S RIGHTS: If you have read this form and have decided to participate in this project, please understand your participation is voluntary and you have the right to withdraw your consent or discontinue participation at any time without penalty or loss of benefits to which you are otherwise entitled. The alternative is not to participate. You have the right to refuse to answer particular questions. The results of this research study may be presented at scientific or professional meetings or published in scientific journals. Your individual privacy will be maintained in all published and written data resulting from the study. In accordance with scientific norms, the data from this study may be used or shared with other researchers for future research (after removing personally identifying information) without additional consent from you.

CONTACT INFORMATION:
Questions: If you have any questions, concerns or complaints about this research, its procedures, risks and benefits, contact the Protocol Director, Myra Cheng (myra@cs.stanford.edu)

Independent Contact: If you are not satisfied with how this study is being conducted, or if you have any concerns, complaints, or general questions about the research or your rights as a participant, please contact the Stanford Institutional Review Board (IRB) to speak to someone independent of the research team at 650-723-2480 or toll free at 1-866-680-2906, or email at irbnonmed@stanford.edu. You can also write to the Stanford IRB, Stanford University, 1705 El Camino Real, Palo Alto, CA 94306.
